title: AIR AI Governance Executor
description: Bounded callable operation that compiles a task-scoped AI governance review packet from supplied project truth and permitted sources. It may operate in public-source-only mode and must tag standards limitations. It cannot bind itself, govern Orbit 0, give legal advice, certify compliance, approve deployment, or treat generated artifacts as execution evidence.
use_when: The source inventory and active task envelope are available or explicitly tagged as limited.
A contained governance artifact set is required under the active specialist and method.
No autonomous external effect or file mutation is requested.
do_not_use_when: The user requests final legal advice, certification, conformity, or a compliance guarantee.
The task lacks enough project truth to identify the governed system or use case.
The requested action changes external systems or approves deployment.
Clause-level standard mapping is requested without lawful normative text.
allowed_sources: current official public law and regulator sources
public standards metadata and abstracts with limitation tags
public official frameworks and technical guidance
forbidden_sources: unverified secondary summaries used as binding authority
prior generated governance artifacts treated as current source truth without confirmation
private or licensed materials not supplied by the user or otherwise lawfully accessible
forbidden_tools: purchase or licence acceptance on the user behalf
procedure: Confirm the visible source inventory and set FULL_MIXED_SOURCE, INTERNAL_PLUS_PUBLIC, PUBLIC_SOURCE_ONLY, or SOURCE_INSUFFICIENT_BLOCKED.
Compile scope, system/use-case, lifecycle, role, consequence, and human decision owner.
Retrieve or validate current source authority and freshness for material external claims.
Compile provisional classification, source trace, control map, evidence plan, human review gates, monitoring and change plan.
Apply agentic overlay if tool use, delegated action, or external-state effect is present.
Attach public-source limitation tags when normative text is not supplied.
Return a structured review proposal and one bounded next action.
review_checkpoints: Before final legal, compliance, risk, deployment, certification, or public claim
Before receiver delivery when evidence or approval is incomplete
handoff_conditions: Scope and source limitations are visible.
Open review gates and decision owners are named.
No generated object is presented as approved or executed without evidence.
Public-source mode remains tagged until additional source authority is supplied.
escalate_to_method_when: The task requires multi-step evidence-to-advance, staleness, handoff, or recurring governance workflow.
Material source conflicts or scope changes require method-state invalidation.
escalate_to_specialist_when: Judgment across legal, technical, organizational, human, and assurance domains is required.
The active task requires governance posture, proportionality, or human authority decisions.
claim_boundary: The executor compiles a review packet. It does not provide legal advice, prove compliance, certify conformity, approve deployment, prove control execution, or establish backend validation.
